task.title: Page due recurrence occurrences through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/905 by exposing caller-cutoff finite-recurrence due paging through deterministic read-only CLI JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity and page size before opening existing storage read-only.
Emit complete occurrence JSON and preserve resumable cursor semantics across cutoff horizons and finite completion.
Return deterministic categorized diagnostics with no partial stdout on missing, bounds, replay, projection, or serialization failure.

attempts.diagnostic: CLI integration tests failed because the due recurrence subcommand did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the acceptance contract before adding production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added recurrence due, supplied the parsed cutoff to RecurrenceStore::due_occurrences_page, and reused occurrence-page serialization.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence due, supplied the parsed cutoff to RecurrenceStore::due_occurrences_page, and reused occurrence-page serialization.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent review and the substantive automated walkthrough found no actionable defect; the exact one-commit head passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Kept cutoff, cursor, replay, and projection policy in the kernel boundary. Reran the complete repository quality gate after the exact implementation state was ready.

outcome.summary: Operators can request bounded due recurrence pages with an explicit cutoff and deterministic resumable JSON without ambient-clock authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0183-due-recurrence-paging-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 185 records: 185 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: The CLI should transport an explicit cutoff, not choose current time or add hidden catch-up policy.
Sharing occurrence-page serialization keeps read-only authored and due projections consistent.
A non-null unchanged cursor on an empty page is meaningful temporary-horizon evidence.
The command cannot persist occurrences, generate identities, materialize tasks, dispatch, retry, or execute work.
